public_comment.topic: Spoke in support of the restoration budget and the forthcoming override, cautioning that cuts are far harder to restore than to make and that the committee should wait until the actual need is known before alarming the public.

minutes.headline: Committee advanced a "needs" FY27 budget it says the town cannot currently fund without an override
minutes.summary: The School Committee held its FY2027 budget hearing, presenting a restoration (not expansion) budget built around bringing back positions cut the prior year, and stressed repeatedly that this is a need-based budget requiring a town override, not one the town can currently afford. Members voted to send that budget to the finance committee, discussed the shape and size of an eventual override (around $1.8 million, unified and untiered), and separately approved several small grant proposals, a cap on virtual-school enrollment, and the FY26-27 school calendar.

budget_items.what_was_said: The committee reviewed a single warrant covering the stated period; no line-item transfers were presented that meeting.
The presenter gave the FY26 total budget including one-time free cash, split between expenses and salaries.

The $500,000 in free cash voted at town meeting was distributed across health insurance, unemployment insurance, the business manager's salary, and multiple teaching positions across schools to preserve staff for one year.
The special education director stated the current number of students placed out of district, separate from in-district substantially separate program counts.

budget_items.topic: School choice net cost / chapter 70 loss
budget_items.what_was_said: The district receives a set per-pupil amount for incoming school-choice students but loses more in chapter 70 aid and tuition value for students choicing out, making it a net financial loss.
The business manager gave last year's revenue collected in the transportation revolving account from bus fees.
Combined revolving account revenues were estimated in this range, with most of it being state or federal money rather than locally generated funds.

budget_items.topic: Federal Title grants FY26 to FY27
budget_items.what_was_said: Title I, II, and IV federal entitlement grants are all projected to shrink substantially for FY27, with Title I facing roughly a 30% cut.
This was the final year of a two-phase Student Opportunity Act grant that had funded a literacy coach position; no further funding is expected.
Legislators secured one-time earmark funding this year, but the district cannot count on earmark funding recurring at the same level next year.
Health insurance costs are projected to rise 9% for FY27 due to reduced coverage rather than cost containment; the district expects to spend out its FY26 budgeted amount without significant overage.
The FY27 heating budget assumption was based on FY25 actual costs, which the presenter said may have been under-budgeted for FY26.

budget_items.topic: Utilities - electricity actual spend to date
budget_items.what_was_said: Actual electricity expenditures so far this fiscal year were given, described as rising along with residential utility costs.
General transportation costs were budgeted with an assumed increase pending final contracted rates from the bus vendor, benchmarked against other districts' business managers.
The district's third-party technology vendor recommended these annual increases for subscriptions and equipment respectively.

Supply cost increase projections tied to tariffs were revised down from an original estimate, though a member suggested the figure may need to rise again; principals say schools have already depleted stockpiled supplies.
After the budget was first posted, the superintendent and business manager cut this amount by moving the athletic director from full-time to half-time and trimming supply lines across schools.
This is the estimated total cost of all restoration and restructuring positions in the FY27 needs budget, assuming staff take the most expensive health insurance tier.
With the restoration additions the schools would represent roughly this share of the town budget; the committee's informal goal has been to keep the share closer to a lower figure.

budget_items.topic: Health insurance share of school budget
budget_items.what_was_said: Health insurance now makes up a larger share of the total school budget than the prior year, a trend the presenter called concerning.

Committee members discussed a possible override figure in this range to cover the restoration budget, while noting the town does not guarantee the school district retains that increment in future years.
A state grant request for civics materials, learning opportunities, and educator training for grades 8-12.

The district sought approval to redirect previously awarded one-time funds, originally intended for the iReady program, toward decodable readers, high school math materials, and targeted professional learning.
A one-time state grant request to pay teachers hourly for planning time to build middle-school career exploration and high school pathway alignment, ahead of a state mandate.
A grant request for professional development and instructional coaching for PreK-5 educators to strengthen foundational literacy instruction.

transfers.description: $500,000 in FY26 free cash distributed across health insurance, unemployment insurance, salary adjustments, and multiple teaching positions
Reallocation of previously awarded one-time earmark grant funds from iReady toward decodable readers, math materials, and professional learning

decisions.decision: The FY27 recommended budget is explicitly framed as an override/need budget that the town cannot currently fund, not a budget already agreed to by the town.
The committee will begin discussing the specific cuts needed for a balanced budget at the March 18 meeting.
The committee's preference is for one unified, townwide override amount rather than a tiered override structure.
Election Day will remain a day off in the FY26-27 school calendar in case TCP is decommissioned and voting moves into a school building.
Discussion of the custodians/janitors item is deferred to a future meeting for fuller discussion.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to send the finance committee an FY27 budget it says the town cannot fund without an override.
Members said they favor one unified, townwide override rather than separate amounts by school or grade.
The committee will not detail what gets cut to balance the budget without an override until its March 18 meeting.
The committee also approved several grant proposals, capped virtual-school enrollment, and adopted the FY26-27 school calendar.
A speaker during public comment urged the committee to hold off alarming the public until the actual funding need is known.

why_it_matters: This budget is described as restoring positions cut the prior year, and the committee says funding it depends on an override, a vote that would raise property taxes beyond the normal cap.
Residents will not see which specific programs or positions are at risk if the override does not pass until the cuts are laid out at a later meeting.
The grant, enrollment-cap and calendar votes are procedural and do not depend on the override outcome.
watch_next: March 18 School Committee meeting, where the specific cuts needed for a balanced (non-override) budget are to be discussed

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.coverage: official minutes are a summary only
reconciliation.summary: The official minutes confirm every vote our minutes captured and match on outcomes, but they record almost none of the dollar figures, percentages, or discussion detail our minutes pulled from the audio, and they add a few concrete facts (the half-time athletic director, two guest principals, an absent/vacant committee seat) that our minutes missed entirely. The one thing a reader should check first is the committee roster: our minutes list five members present (Tony, Laura, Mandy, Cara, Liz) plus "the chair" separately, while the official minutes show only three seats filled (Chair Sculimbrene, Vice Chair Brzozoski, Secretary Gilman) with one member absent and one seat vacant — "Cara" and "Liz" do not correspond to anyone in the official roster.
